as_told.title: Havana syndrome attributed to Russian microwave weaponry

plain: The claim is that Havana syndrome comes from Russian attacks on Americans going back to the 1980s. Havana syndrome is the name for sudden, unexplained headaches, dizziness and brain injuries reported by US diplomats and spies. Michels says a recent 60 Minutes piece, made with the German magazine Der Spiegel, laid this out. A former senior NSA official named Eric Haseltine refers to the same 60 Minutes interview: "if it's the Russians doing it to us, that's an act of war." In a later episode Michels tells it in his own words, crediting the CIA and the NSA. There he says "Russia and microwave weaponry" are behind it, puts it in the last couple of years and leaves out the 1980s. All three tellings rest on the news report rather than on anything the tellers saw. If true, a foreign power would have been quietly harming American officials for decades.
